raw_record.question_text: For the pair of similar figures, use the given areas to find the scale factor of the blue to the green figure.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: the blue rectangle has area 72 m^2 and the green rectangle has area 50 m^2; the figures are stated to be similar. To find the scale factor from the blue figure to the green figure, use the rule that for similar figures, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding lengths. Compute the blue-to-green area ratio as 72/50 = 36/25, then take the square root to get the blue-to-green linear scale factor: sqrt(36/25) = 6/5.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For similar figures, area scale factor = (linear scale factor)^2, so the linear scale factor is the square root of the area ratio.
